task.goal: Produce a single-frame, portrait-anchored premium SuperVisual that pairs an authenticated host portrait with a structured broadcast-metadata stack (date, time, platform, live status) and a lower-band topic/guest line, so a scheduled show moment reads as a specific host's appointment-to-view rather than a generic event flyer.
task.success_condition: The host portrait occupies the dominant right-side visual mass at near-full bleed; the black-plate metadata stack (calendar/date, LIVE badge, platform icon) sits legibly against a neon-accent contrast ratio exceeding 4.5:1; the lower black band carries the episode topic and guest line as the terminal read; the show's own brand mark (wordmark plus logo) appears exactly once and is not upstaged by any secondary product or sponsor mark visible in the portrait crop.
task.atomic_boundary: One scheduled episode/broadcast moment becomes one portrait-anchored premium SuperVisual frame. No multi-slide carousel, no animation, no video edit, and no text-only quote-dominant layout without a portrait subject (that boundary belongs to the Standard tier, not this one).

source_expression_moment.description: The episode's authenticated topic/headline moment to render in the lower black band (e.g. the on-flyer episode premise and guest attribution).

voice_context.description: Host and brand voice/typographic context (recurring host name lockup, network name, accent color system, logo mark) governing rendering decisions for this recurring show.

supervisual_frame.description: A single production-ready portrait-anchored announcement frame with embedded metadata stack and lower-band topic/guest text.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer's feed is full of interchangeable 'upcoming live' announcement graphics; this one must be recognized as this specific host's appointment-to-view through her portrait and the show's consistent brand system, not read as one more generic event flyer.
activative_input.stance: Warm authority - an invitation from a familiar host, not a cold event notice.
stakes: the host's face and the episode topic separate in the viewer's memory
LIVE urgency reads as generic template rather than a real appointment
a secondary product or sponsor mark upstages the host's own brand mark
identity_urges: know exactly when and where to show up
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer sees the host's face first, reads the live/date/time/platform stack second, and reads the topic and guest line as the reason to attend third - then marks the appointment.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer commits to watching live at the stated time because they recognize the host and want to hear this specific topic with this specific guest.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Save the date and time or set a reminder for the live broadcast.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let the metadata stack (date, LIVE badge, platform icon) migrate off the solid black plate onto the photographic portrait region - contrast and legibility break the moment those icons sit over skin tone or fabric texture instead of solid black.

Do not shrink or crop the host portrait below roughly half the frame - this Premium tier is portrait-anchored, unlike the Standard tier's text-only quote card; collapsing the portrait erases the tier distinction and misreads as the wrong sub-format.

Do not render the LIVE badge and the episode topic headline in the same visual weight - LIVE must always carry the highest urgency-coded treatment (badge, not body text), or a live appointment misreads as recorded/past content, or vice versa.

Do not let a secondary brand or product placement visible inside the portrait crop (e.g. an apron logo, a sponsor mark) get duplicated, enlarged, or repositioned into the black band - sponsor content is incidental to the frame, never the activation subject.

Do not replace the recurring two-tone host name lockup (accent-color first line, solid-white second line) with a single-color treatment - that lockup is the recurring identity anchor across every episode in this series, and altering it breaks episode-to-episode host recognition.
